reason: The vestibular aqueduct abnormality defines an inner-ear disorder. Its location within the temporal bone does not independently establish musculoskeletal damage.

Lysosomal neurodegeneration supports neurologic and metabolic_endocrine primary labels. Neurogenic bladder causes urinary loss of function in 2/3. Respiratory insufficiency and cortical visual impairment do not establish intrinsic pulmonary or ocular damage.
Skeletal and dental developmental defects define the disease. Hearing impairment in 30-79% supports otologic involvement; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Neither the primary organ nor a consistent metastatic organ is specified. Assigning a particular organ axis would be speculative; the label appropriately records this uncertainty.
Deficient T-cell development and lymphopenia support both infectious_immune and haematologic primary labels. Other organ manifestations are occasional or attributable to separate infections.

Autoinflammation establishes infectious_immune. The supplied rash, organomegaly and hypertriglyceridemia do not demonstrate persistent skin injury, organ dysfunction or a defining metabolic disorder; the parent flag alone is insufficient.
The definition explicitly places tumor origin in the liver. Osteoid-producing histology does not imply a skeletal primary site or skeletal involvement.
This is a localized dental disorder, covered by gastrointestinal. Tooth-to-alveolar-bone fusion does not establish an independent locomotor disorder; limb abnormalities are occasional.
The pyriform sinus is part of the hypopharynx, which the guide explicitly assigns to pulmonary. Tumor occupation establishes the primary axis.

The metabolic defect and defining neonatal liver disease support the primary labels. Neurologic impairment at 80-99% and cataracts at 30-79% support involvement. The four-axis cap reasonably excludes coagulopathy.
